question: What does a fasting blood sugar test primarily measure?

options.A: Baseline blood glucose after food restriction
options.B: Maximum blood glucose right after a heavy meal
options.C: Average blood sugar over the last three months
options.D: Total amount of insulin stored in the pancreas

explanation: The test measures glucose levels when the body has not consumed calories for several hours, showing the true resting baseline. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is it important to test blood sugar while a patient is fasting?

options.A: It makes the red blood cells easier to see under a microscope.
options.B: It forces the pancreas to release all remaining insulin stores.
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling dizzy during the blood draw.
options.D: It removes the temporary glucose spikes caused by recent eating.

explanation: Food intake naturally raises blood sugar temporarily, so fasting gives a clear baseline without dietary interference. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which pancreatic hormone lowers blood sugar by helping cells take in glucose?
explanation: Insulin acts as the primary hormone that allows body cells to absorb glucose from the bloodstream, thereby lowering blood sugar. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the primary role of glucagon during a fasting state?

options.A: To signal the liver to release stored glucose into the blood
options.B: To help the pancreas produce more beta cells for energy
options.C: To block insulin from entering the muscle tissues
options.D: To transport excess sugar directly to the kidneys for excretion

explanation: When fasting lowers blood sugar, glucagon tells the liver to break down stored glycogen to keep blood sugar from dropping too low. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which symptom is a classic indicator that prompts a doctor to order a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Sudden low blood pressure and dizziness
options.C: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles
options.D: Yellowing of the skin and eyes

explanation: Polydipsia and polyuria are hallmark signs of high blood sugar that signal the need for diagnostic screening. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h3)

question: A healthy pregnant woman at 26 weeks gestation goes for her routine antenatal clinic. Why is a glucose screening typically included?

options.A: To check for gestational diabetes that can develop during pregnancy
options.B: To confirm the exact gestational age of the growing fetus
options.C: To test her kidney function against pregnancy hormones
options.D: To measure how much iron she is storing in her liver

explanation: Pregnancy hormones can cause insulin resistance, making routine screening for gestational diabetes essential during the second trimester. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the minimum recommended fasting time before a fasting blood sugar test?
explanation: A minimum of 8 hours without caloric intake is required to ensure the digestive system is at rest and baseline glucose can be measured. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which beverage is generally allowed during the fasting period prior to the test?
explanation: Plain water has no calories or active compounds that stimulate digestion, keeping the fasting state intact while preventing dehydration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h4)

question: What special chemical is added to the blood collection tube for a fasting blood sugar test to keep the blood cells from eating up the sugar?
explanation: Great job! Sodium fluoride acts as a preservative (glycolytic inhibitor) that stops red blood cells from consuming the glucose in the tube before the lab technician can test it. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h5)

question: When should the nurse label the collected blood specimen tube?

options.A: At the bedside immediately after the blood draw
options.B: Inside the laboratory before handing it to the technician
options.C: At the nursing station after finishing all morning rounds
options.D: Before entering the patient room to save time

explanation: Labeling specimens at the bedside immediately after collection ensures proper patient identification and prevents mislabeling errors. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the standard normal fasting blood sugar range for a healthy adult?
explanation: A fasting blood sugar reading under 100 mg/dL is considered normal for individuals without metabolic disorders. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h6)

question: A patient's fasting blood sugar result comes back at 115 mg/dL. How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: It is completely normal and requires no further follow-up.
options.B: It indicates prediabetes or impaired fasting glucose.
options.C: It confirms that the patient has full-blown Type 1 diabetes.
options.D: It shows severe hypoglycemia requiring immediate sugar intake.

explanation: Values between 100 and 125 mg/dL fall into the prediabetes range, signaling a need for lifestyle changes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h6)

question: What term is used to describe a dangerously low fasting blood sugar level?
explanation: Hypoglycemia refers to blood glucose levels falling below the normal healthy threshold, typically under 70 mg/dL. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h7)

question: A patient with diabetes has a fasting blood sugar of 55 mg/dL and is shaky and confused. What is the most likely cause of these symptoms?

options.A: Kidney failure causing a backup of metabolic waste
options.B: A normal reaction to an overnight fasting period
options.C: Dehydration from drinking too much plain water
options.D: Brain glucose deprivation from low blood sugar

explanation: When blood sugar drops too low, the brain lacks energy, causing neurological symptoms like confusion and shaking. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h7)

question: Why can severe physical stress or a sudden infection cause a high fasting blood sugar reading?

options.A: Infection causes the kidneys to stop filtering sugar out of the blood.
options.B: Dehydration turns blood cells into pure glucose molecules.
options.C: Fever completely destroys insulin molecules stored in the pancreas.
options.D: Stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline are released, raising blood glucose.

explanation: You've got this! Acute stress triggers your body to release hormones that push stored glucose into the bloodstream to give you energy for a fight-or-flight response. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h8)

question: Which medication class is well known for increasing blood sugar levels during therapy?
explanation: Corticosteroids stimulate hepatic glucose production and induce insulin resistance, frequently raising blood sugar levels. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h8)

question: What is the most important immediate nursing action after a fasting blood draw for a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Provide food and allow the patient to take held morning medications.
options.B: Send the patient home immediately without checking the puncture site.
options.C: Instruct the patient to continue fasting until the lab results return.
options.D: Encourage the patient to run on a treadmill to lower blood sugar.

explanation: Well done! Because the patient fasted and held their morning diabetes drugs, they need food and their routine medications right away to prevent their blood sugar from crashing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h9)

question: What key lifestyle advice should a nurse include when educating a patient with prediabetes?

options.A: Avoid all types of physical movement to preserve energy
options.B: Sleep for at least fourteen hours every single night
options.C: Incorporate a balanced diet and regular physical activity
options.D: Eliminate all forms of water from the daily diet

explanation: Dietary changes and regular exercise help improve insulin sensitivity and prevent prediabetes from advancing to full diabetes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h9)
